findings.claim: The brief states the paper's theorems as: Thakur indices span Z_w; 'the smaller family with every entry<q is independent at every weight; consequently the Thakur family is a basis and dim Z_w=d(w) for 1≤w≤2q−2'. Theorem D is not a consequence of Theorems A and B. For q > 2 and q < w ≤ 2q−2, T⁰_w is a proper subset of T_w. For example, at q = 3 and w = 4, |T_4| = d(4) = 6 but |T⁰_4| = 5 (the compositions of 4 into parts 1 and 2), so A and B give only 5 ≤ dim_K Z_4 ≤ 6. The paper proves Theorem D from Theorem 6.2 (independence of the family T′_w of indices with no entry divisible by q, for q > 2 and w ≤ 2q−2), Lemma 6.1 (|T′_w| = |T_w|) and Theorem A. The brief's list of 'theorems from this source' also omits Theorem 6.2 and Corollary C, although the brief is meant to state the final theorems as the paper does. Severity set to high by the coordinator: the brief's derivation is false, not just incomplete. The coordinator checked the manuscript: p. 4 says "When q > 2, contrary to Corollary C, Theorem D needs both the algebraic part and the transcendental part", and p. 5 that Theorem D follows from a lower bound for a different set T′_w (Theorem 6.2, p. 22). A design job following the brief would plan Theorem D from Theorems A and B, which cannot work for q < w ≤ 2q − 2. A false brief statement is high. Also: The brief states the paper's final theorems as: Theorem A; 'the smaller family with every entry<q is independent at every weight; consequently the Thakur family is a basis and dim Z_w=d(w) for 1≤w≤2q−2.' The 'consequently' is false. Theorems A and B together give a basis only for w≤q (Corollary C). For q<w≤2q−2 the small-entry family is strictly smaller than the Thakur family, so A and B give only |I^0_w| ≤ dim_K Z_w ≤ d(w). Example: q=3, w=4. I^0_4 consists of the 5 compositions of 4 into parts 1 and 2. The Thakur family I^T_4={(1,1,1,1),(1,1,2),(1,2,1),(2,1,1),(2,2),(3,1)} has d(4)=d(3)+d(2)+d(1)=3+2+1=6 members. Theorem D rests on Theorem 6.2 (for q>2 and w≤2q−2 the MZVs with no entry divisible by q are K-linearly independent) and on Lemma 6.1 (|T_w|=|T′_w|). The brief never states Theorem 6.2, and it omits Corollary C. It mentions only ingredients of 'the final range extension'. A design job that follows the brief's statement of the final theorems would plan Theorem D as a corollary of A and B and omit the theorem it actually needs. The extraction's summary and the report's table state the logic correctly, so the brief contradicts them.

findings.claim: The paper asserts that the Anderson–Thakur polynomials are integral: 'α_n(t) ∈ A[t]' (p. 17), so that H_n ∈ A[t]. The item AT-polynomials only defines α_n by the generating series, and no item states integrality. A priori Γ_n·[x^{n−1}](…) lies in K[t] = F_q(θ)[t]. After θ and t are swapped, H_n lies in F_q(t)[θ] and may have poles at roots of unity t ∈ F̄_q, which lie on the unit circle. So without integrality H_n need not lie in K̄[t], or even in T. Integrality is needed for Φ_s ∈ Mat_{r+1}(K̄[t]) (single-motive-matrix, prefix-Phi, the ABP hypothesis, the MZ property) and for the Gauss norm ‖H_n‖ in AT-bound. The source AT-bound cites, Chang 2014 Theorem 5.5.1, opens with exactly this statement. The proof is elementary. The x^{n−1} coefficient is a sum over compositions of n−1 into powers q^j with multiplicities m_j, each with denominator ∏ D_j^{m_j}. Carrying q copies of q^j into one q^{j+1} replaces D_j^q by D_{j+1} = [j+1]D_j^q, a multiple. So every denominator divides the carry-free one ∏ D_j^{n_j} = Γ_n. I computed α_n exactly from the generating series for q = 2 (n ≤ 12) and q = 3 (n ≤ 14). All of them lie in A[t], with deg_θ H_n < nq/(q−1). For example, H_3 = t + θ² at q = 2, and H_4 = −t³ − t − θ³ and H_5 = θ³ − t at q = 3.

findings.claim: The non-example test says 'Checking d≥0 alone is weaker than the stated all-integer predicate, because d=−1 tests the shifted boundary.' For a weight-w family (w ≥ 1), the d = −1 equation says only that β vanishes on the one depth-one index (w): every S_{−1} is 0, and S_0(t) is 1 for t = (w) and 0 otherwise. If the equations hold for all d ≥ 0, summing them gives Σα_sζ_A(s) + Σβ_tζ_A(t) = β_(w). By Chang's theorem that 1 is K̄-linearly independent of any K-independent set of MZVs of positive weight, β_(w) = 0. So the two predicates are equivalent, and the 'weaker' claim has no witness: a formaliser cannot exhibit a family that satisfies d ≥ 0 and fails d = −1.

findings.claim: Both texts say the maximal-weight coefficients B_t are killed by 'lower-weight algebraic independence'. The input the paper uses, and the only one the induction provides, is linear independence over K̄ of the lower-weight MZVs ζ_A(t), t∈I(w0). This is Theorem B (or 6.2) at weight w0<w, upgraded from K to K̄ by Chang's descent. Algebraic independence is a much stronger property that neither the induction hypothesis nor any item supplies. The item's own statement correctly says 'linearly independent over K, hence over K̄ by MZ-descent', so its proof step contradicts its statement.
findings.evidence: The paper (p. 18): 'Suppose that for w′ < w MZV's in T0w′ are all linearly independent over K, hence over K by [9, Proposition 4.3.1].' The second K carries a bar on the page image. The paper (p. 20): 'Specializing (5.5) at t = θ^{q^j} and using (5.4) yields Σ_{t∈I(w0)} Bt(θ^{q^j})(L(t)(θ))^{q^j} = 0 for j ≫ 1. Since w0 < w, by the induction hypothesis we deduce that Bt(θ^{q^j}) = 0'. That is a K̄-linear relation after taking q^j-th roots. The report reads: 'Maximal prefix weights are eliminated by specializing along the Frobenius orbit and using lower-weight algebraic independence.'

Membership in E also requires every coefficient to lie in K̄, and nothing in the item or its dependencies (C-infinity, entire-ring, twist) supplies that. The ABP application in §5.2 needs it, because ψ has entries L(t)Ω^{w−w(t)} and must lie in E^{|I|+1}. The coefficients are infinite sums (for example the t-coefficient involves Σ_{i≥1}θ^{−q^i}), so algebraicity is not automatic. It does follow directly from the functional equation. Write Ω=Σc_n t^n. Comparing coefficients in Ω^(−1)=(t−θ)Ω gives c_n^{1/q}=c_{n−1}−θc_n, so θ^q c_n^q+c_n−c_{n−1}^q=0, with c_{−1}=0 and c_0=(−θ)^{−q/(q−1)}. By induction every c_n is algebraic over K.
